sources.title: On Context-Free Languages
sources.locator: Manfred Kufleitner, Yet another proof of Parikh's Theorem, arXiv:2210.02925v1, Corollary 2, page 4
sources.checked_implication: The Parikh image of a context-free language is semilinear. Unary length images therefore have eventual periodicity.
sources.application: Canonical lengths have irrational natural density, so cannot be eventually periodic; intersection with a regular canonical selector transfers the obstruction to the full fibre.
sources.access_note: The original ACM PDF returned403; the exact statement and proof were checked in the named primary alternative, not inferred from snippets.

sources.title: Über Potenzreihen mit ganzzahligen Koeffizienten
sources.locator: Bell, Miles and Ward, Towards a Pólya–Carlson dichotomy for algebraic dynamics, arXiv:1307.2369v1, page2, named Pólya–Carlson theorem
sources.checked_implication: Integer coefficients and radius one give the rational-or-natural-boundary dichotomy.
sources.application: The canonical series has infinitely many binary coefficients and radius one. Its irrational support density excludes rationality.
sources.additional_reading: https://people.math.ethz.ch/~airibar/Polya_Carlson.pdf, Theorem6 and historical references; no claim of having read Carlson's original German publication.

sources.title: Differentiably Finite Power Series
sources.locator: Definition1.1 and Theorem1.2, printed page175; author-hosted scan inspected visually
sources.checked_implication: D-finite series satisfy a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients.
sources.application: Ordinary-point continuation confines finite singularities to a finite polynomial-zero set, incompatible with a natural boundary. Algebraic functions are D-finite by finite-dimensional differentiation over the algebraic extension.
